children: Meta Platforms
and Snap
are set to face a fresh legal test over allegations that their social media platforms contributed to mental health problems among young users, with jury selection beginning Wednesday in Los Angeles.

The trial involves two plaintiffs who allege that features such as autoplay and endless scrolling encouraged compulsive use, contributing to depression, anxiety, and eating disorders. The proceedings are expected to last several weeks, with Meta
Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg, Instagram head Adam Mosseri, and Snap
CEO Evan Spiegel expected to testify.
The case is the second individual-plaintiff trial over claims that social media companies deliberately designed their platforms to be addictive. In March, a Los Angeles

The current proceedings cover both plaintiffs’ claims against Snap
and the Mississippi plaintiff’s claims against Meta
. The Illinois plaintiff settled her claims against Meta, while both plaintiffs reached settlements with TikTok (
) and YouTube
before trial.
Meta
argues that factors beyond its platforms contributed to the plaintiffs’ difficulties and says it has introduced protections for young users. Snap
maintains that Snapchat differs from traditional social media feeds and that the allegations misrepresent its design and safeguards.

The cases are among thousands of lawsuits consolidated in Los Angeles Superior Court. Their outcomes could influence how other claims are resolved. The companies argue that Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act shields them from liability, but the trial judge has allowed the platform-design claims to proceed.
